intro:
Use it to choose one of a few options that are easier to see than to name: a pointer style, a canvas size, a background, an export quality. Each card leads with a picture of the option and its name sits under it.

It suits two to six options. Past that the pictures get too small to compare; use a [Select](/docs/web/components/select) with icons instead. For options that are only words, use [Tabs](/docs/web/components/tabs) or a radio group.

Give the group an `aria-label`, or point `aria-labelledby` at its heading, so a screen reader says what is being chosen.

parts.Item: One option. Its `value` is what the group is set to when it is chosen. The chosen card is ringed in the group's colour and a check appears in its corner.
parts.Media: The picture of the option: a drawing, an icon or an image, centred in a rounded frame at the group's `aspect`. An image fills it edge to edge. On the chosen card it grows slightly.
parts.Label: The option's name, under the picture. It is also what a screen reader calls the card.
parts.Description: A line under the name: what the option costs or what it is for. A screen reader reads it after the name.

examples.title: Shapes
examples.description: `aspect` sets the shape of every card's picture. Here square pictures hold a frame drawn at each ratio, so the options can be compared at a glance.

examples.title: Images
examples.description: Anything that fills the media fills it to the edge, so a gradient, a photo or a video still works as the picture. `columns` sets how many cards stand in a row.

examples.title: With descriptions
examples.description: A `ChoiceCards.Description` under the label says what the option costs. `color` sets the ring and the check; here `info`.

notes:
### Keyboard

The group is one stop in the tab order. The arrow keys move the choice from card to card, and Space chooses the focused one.

### Columns

Without `columns`, the cards share one row, up to four of them. Set `columns` for a grid, and use a narrower count on a small screen by passing it from your own breakpoint.

### Forms

Give it a `name` and it submits the chosen `value` with the form it is in. `required` stops the form being sent before a card is chosen.

With reduced motion turned on, the check and the picture change without moving.
